acceptance: The GitHub cache is available without the HTTP feature, never creates directories during reads, verifies regular non-symlink files, and returns a safe absolute entry path for offline module loading.

A previously fetched GitHub root snapshot can resolve its complete pinned graph from an explicit cache without network access; remote sources remain PackageSource::GitHub while physical paths stay in the path map.
check, run, build, and disasm accept --package-cache <dir>, require aipo.lock, reject missing/corrupt cache entries without fetching, and use the verified graph for module loading.
Digest, source, version, dependency-edge, capability and target mismatches fail closed as package diagnostics; no network or global cache is introduced.
Positive and negative tests cover cache path safety, offline graph loading, stale locks, missing artifacts, CLI flag parsing and existing local-only behavior; full repository gates remain green.

amendments.reason: Register the approved cache-aware offline consumption scope before certification

evidence.description: aipo-package default tests passed 45 cases and all-features tests passed 48 cases, including non-creating cache reads, regular-file/symlink rejection, safe entry paths, recursive offline graph resolution and cache reuse.

aipo-cli package integration tests passed 19 cases by default and 20 with github-http, covering check/run/build/disasm cache consumption, missing cache failure, stale locks, flag forms and duplicate rejection.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets and cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features passed; the default dependency tree contains no ureq.

cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo doc default/all-features, node selftest, cargo deny, cargo audit, prumo validate and prumo doctor all passed.
CLI reference, ADP-007 and GitHub fetch security documentation now define --package-cache, read-only cache behavior, lock requirements, diagnostics and the no-network boundary.
